Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

suppose verb

for the sake of argument

also suppose that, supposing, let’s suppose, let’s say, what if, for the sake of argument

classical

Cic. Tusc. 1.82: fac … animōs nōn remanēre post mortem
Cic. Fam. 7.23.1: fac, quaesō, quī ego sum esse tē

fac (+ accusative and infinitive)

imperative of faciō, with an accusative and infinitive

suppose, say (that)

Lewis & Short: fac, used hypothetically, “suppose, assume”. Not fac ut, make sure that (see sure).

Other words

  • fingō, fingere, fīnxī, fictum — suppose, imagine (that)

    verb, third conjugation, with an accusative and infinitive: finge, fingāmus · also used · classical · Cic. Ac. 2.117: finge aliquem nunc fierī sapientem, nōndum esse; Quint. 1.1.24: fingāmus igitur Alexandrum darī nōbīs

  • quid sī …? — what if …?

    with the subjunctive of a supposed case · also used · classical · Ter. Eun. 368: Quid sī nunc tūte fortūnātus fīās?

Examples

  • sed fac, ut istī volunt, animōs nōn remanēre post mortem

    but suppose, as those people would have it, that souls do not survive deathCic. Tusc. 1.82

  • fingāmus igitur Alexandrum darī nōbīs impositum gremiō, dignum tantā cūrā īnfantem (quamquam suus cuique dignus est)

    so let us imagine that an Alexander is given to us and laid in our lap, a baby worthy of so much care (though everyone’s own child is worthy of it)Quint. 1.1.24

  • Quid sī nunc tūte fortūnātus fīās?

    What if you were the lucky one now?Ter. Eun. 368

See also assume, imagine, example, think.
